title: Face-wheel drive with a crank slide
intent: From the frame, determine whether rotor C turns and slide Y travels at the illustrated instant by tracing the selected face and the independent keyed crank.

choices.reason: For C to stay still, B must turn CCW and overrun the CW-locking clutch. For Y to go right, the top pin on the keyed crank K must sweep to the right.
For C to turn CW, B must turn CW and engage the clutch. The solid key also turns K clockwise, sending its upper pin and the horizontal slide to the right.
The brake can hold C when B turns CCW. Treating that brake as a stop for Y ignores the separate solid key from A to K and the horizontal velocity of the upper pin.
CW motion of C requires the clutch to engage. A stationary Y would require zero pin travel across its slot, but a clockwise crank carries its top pin horizontally at this instant.
